attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed as his assertion.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the late-December timing, the 'apparently' and 'roughly' hedges, and the 'big leagues' wording. The core cost and capability assertions are firm observations about DeepSeek-V3.

contract.note: Reading 'roughly 1/50th' as about 2% of earlier frontier training costs on a comparable basis is a fair, ordinary reading. Marcus named no denominator or accounting basis, though, so the result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: DeepSeek's own report: about $5.6M at rental rates, final training only, with claims of competitive benchmarks. This is a company disclosure with no comparison model, so it cannot confirm the 1/50th ratio or independently confirm near-frontier performance.
Epoch's methodology note shows that cost estimates use different bases (depreciation vs rental vs total development). It is published before V3 and contains no V3 comparison.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only DeepSeek's self-reported final-run rental cost and its own benchmark claims. No earlier model is named as the comparison and there is no common cost basis, so the roughly 1/50th ratio can be neither confirmed nor refuted. Near-frontier performance rests only on the company's own disclosure. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: A plain factual observation: no public GPT-5 existed as of the 26 Jan 2025 post date.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'no public GPT-5 release by the post date' is the ordinary reading and is fair to Marcus.

evidence.note: OpenAI's release record, dated 7 Aug 2025, introduces GPT-5 as a new model. That puts the first public release after 26 Jan 2025. This is the release record the contract prefers, and it is dated before the evaluation date.
Reporting from 20 Jan 2025 treats GPT-5 as a future, unreleased upgrade. This agrees with the claim six days before the post.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own launch record dates GPT-5's public introduction to 7 Aug 2025. Reporting from 20 Jan 2025 describes it as not yet released. Nothing shows a release on or before 26 Jan 2025. Together these establish that GPT-5 was not publicly available on the post date.
